parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
Last year my family and I started to make our own fruit and vegetable garden. We wanted to do something for our planet so we decided to grow our own plants organically. This means that we only use natural ways to look after them. For example, we put our old fruit and vegetables on the ground where the plants grow, but other people just throw all their old food in the bin. Also, now we grow our own fruit and vegetables, so we don't need to buy them.

Having an organic garden is clearly a healthier option because the fruit and vegetables you grow will be safe for people and animals, too. We had to work very hard. At first, we were afraid because we might not have enough time to do everything, but then we realised that each of us could look after the garden on different days.

To make our garden we used a large wooden box which was about the size of our kitchen table. We cleaned it and made 20 holes at the bottom for the water to drain out. We covered the holes with some little stones and the soil where the plants could grow.

Then we planted very tiny plants and watered them every day. On the left we planted tomatoes, onions, carrots and potatoes, while on the right there were a few melons and strawberries. In about a month we picked our first fruits and vegetables. We were so excited when he had them for dinner!

options.C: to stop making so much rubbish

What does Larry say about the fruits and vegetables he planted?

options.A: The vegetables and fruit were in different parts.
options.B: The plants were very small, but delicious.
options.C: They first ate the fruit, then the vegetables.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a teacher telling her students about a week at the Arts Centre they take part in.
parts.transcript:
Right everyone. Just some information on The Arts Centre that is open from July to September. You will leave at half past nine on the 17th and get there in about half an hour. During the week you will spend there, you will have several activities to choose from: students can do painting or drawing from 8 a.m. to midday, while after lunch those who are interested can try dancing or photography.
The courses are available for students aged 11 to 15, but remember your parents have to fill in a form where they agree to let you do the courses.
During the week at the Arts Centre you will also be able to take part in weekend activities: Unfortunately we won't be able to take you to the swimming pool as we did last year but we will go on a trip to London and visit museums as well. The cost of the week, which includes accommodation and meals, is 139 pounds, so please remember to bring the money by Thursday.

What did Adam learn at the course?

parts.transcript:
Girl: Hi Adam. Jessie told me you've decided to learn how to cook. How is the course you're doing?
Adam: Well, it was my mother who told me to do it. At first I thought it wouldn't be so interesting as I don't want to be a chef like her. But half an hour after the class started, I realised it was a great opportunity: you know how I love good food, so making dishes can be great fun.
Girl: I'm sure it was great way to spend the day.
Adam: It was! And being in a kitchen from morning to evening was a very interesting experience. After the first half hour when the teacher told us what to use, it took me only three hours to make a very special meal with very simple foods such as cheese, vegetables and eggs. When I got back in the evening I was really happy about the results.
Girl: Was the kitchen large?
Adam: Very large. There were 14 of us, but we had enough space to work.
Girl: So are you going to the course on desserts next month?
Adam: I'd love to, but I don't think I'll have enough time because next month I have a lot of tests. Anyway I'd like to keep working in the kitchen by myself. I'd like to try to make a meal for my vegetarian grandmother. She really loves trying new dishes so I'll see what I can do: I have an interesting cookbook with a lot of wonderful vegetable dishes!
Girl: Sounds great! I hope you'll invite me too.

parts.title: Listening - Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Kevin talking to his father about a science project. What will each classmate do?
parts.transcript:
Kevin: Hey Dad, can you help me do some research on monkeys? We're doing a science project on wild animals and I've got to write a few pages for next week.
Dad: Sure. What are your classmates doing?
Kevin: Well, my best friend Jason has the most interesting project: he has to study spiders. You know I love spiders.
Dad: How about Amanda? I know she really likes horse riding. Is she going to write about horses?
Kevin: No, actually she chose penguins because her father took some photos when he was in Antarctica. And Lenny has already finished his project on fish.
Dad: Is Phil doing his research on lions? I know he loves big cats.
Kevin: Yes, he is. And Sally wants to study bees: she wants to tell us how they make honey.
Dad: That's interesting!
